metadata.note: Locations are best-effort approximations built from public sources (Wikipedia, Hunt Midwest, Missouri DGLS geologic field-trip guides, KCUR, KSHB). Polygon outlines are ILLUSTRATIVE extents, not surveyed mine boundaries, unless 'confidence' is 'verified'. See README.md for how to replace these with authoritative GIS data.
sources: https://share.mo.gov/nr/mgs (Missouri Geological Survey field trip guides)

properties.name: SubTropolis
properties.notes: World's largest underground business complex. Room-and-pillar mine, 25-ft pillars, ~65-70F year round. USPS and EPA Region 7 lease space here. North of the Missouri River, Clay County side.

properties.name: Parkville Commercial Underground
properties.notes: Former limestone mine beneath a bluff near Park University; houses a whiskey distillery and other tenants. Exact underground footprint not public.

properties.name: Brunson Instrument / 87th & Blue River area mine
properties.notes: One of the first underground sites in the area developed specifically to use mined-out space (moved underground 1961 for vibration-free precision instrument calibration).
properties.source: Missouri DGLS geologic field trip guide, 'Geology of Kansas City'

properties.name: J. Rieger & Co. tunnel (West Bottoms)
properties.operator: Historic - Heim Brewery / J. Rieger & Co.
properties.notes: 400-ft tunnel discovered beneath the distillery during renovation, believed linked to the historic Heim Brewery.

properties.name: Independence, MO historic quarries (Shaw / McDonald)
properties.status: historic surface/underground quarry, exact site lost to records
properties.notes: Documented in 1897 Mine, Quarry and Metallurgical Record and Missouri Bureau of Geology and Mines reports. Placed near central Independence pending better georeferencing - do not treat this pin as precise.

properties.name: Community of Christ Temple / Temple Lot area
properties.notes: Reference pin only, added because it's a common orientation point in Independence. No public mine map confirms a void directly beneath this specific footprint. It sits in the same regional limestone belt as other Jackson County mines but on the OPPOSITE side of the Missouri River from SubTropolis - they are not the same mine system.
